title: The Seam Is Not a Horizon
statement: A photographed street supports a divided witness: bronze evidence on one side, an imagined ecology on the other. Their almost-continuous silhouette invites the eye to complete what the cut refuses to join. Beyond them, Earth is a small visible fact within a larger darkness. The seam marks the difference between seeing, completing, and leaving unknown.
brief:
Create an original collage using only the provided source images. There is no target image. Respond to the condition through the composition itself. Give the finished work a title and a short artist statement.

Represent the boundary between what you know, what you infer, and what you cannot know.

notes.note: Begin with a dark, unfilled field and a sharply interrupted bronze portrait. A low photographic strip will ground the fragments in observable detail.

Give the missing half of the portrait a conjectural body made from the animal-flower manuscript. A narrow exposed seam will distinguish this imagined continuation from the bronze evidence, while the surrounding dark field remains open.

The divided portrait and photographic pedestal now read clearly. Refine the bronze cheek edge to remove the remaining studio background, and preserve the open darkness rather than filling it with more symbols.

notes.note: The finished composition holds three distinct registers: photographic detail, an imagined continuation, and open darkness. The narrow seam interrupts the otherwise unified portrait, and the small Earth balances the face without resolving the unknown. No further additions are needed.
